stories.headline: Yankees' Anthony Volpe making debut at third base
stories.summary: Anthony Volpe was set to make his first career big league appearance at third base for the Yankees in the opener of a doubleheader against the Orioles.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- Anthony Volpe was set to make his first career big league appearance at third base for the New York Yankees in the opener of a doubleheader against the Baltimore Orioles on Friday.

Volpe had started 11 games at second base since his recall from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes Barre on Sept. 10.

During his last stint in Triple-A after rookie George Lombard Jr. replaced him as the Yankees shortstop, Volpe started three games at third. He did not commit an error in three chances while batting .284 with 10 homers and 21 RBIs in 28 games.

Volpe was New York's Opening Day shortstop for the 2023-25 seasons but began 2026 on the injured list while recovering from offseason surgery to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder. After his 20-day minor league rehab assignment ended May 3, Volpe was optioned to Triple-A and returned to the Yankees 10 days later when José Caballero fractured his right middle finger.

Volpe, 25, hit a grand slam and drove in a career-high five runs in a memorable return to the big leagues Sept. 10. He is hitting .241 with two homers and 26 RBI in 68 games this year.

Stanton sees 20 pitches

Attempting to return from injuries to calf muscles in both legs, Giancarlo Stanton took on-field batting practice against a minor league pitching and Ryan Weathers, who hopes to come off the injured list for the postseason.

Stanton saw 20 pitches in four at-bats along with Trent Grisham, who has been sidelined since straining his right hamstring Sept. 4. Stanton struck out three times against a minor league pitcher and struck out against Weathers, who is recovering from a strained right forearm.

Stanton hit on the field at Yankee Stadium for the second straight day. He took swings for about 40 minutes against a high-velocity pitching machine Thursday.

He hasn't played since April 24 after starting the season with a .256 batting average, three homers and 14 RBIs in 24 games. If the right-handed-hitting Stanton is on New York's roster for the best-of-three wild-card series that starts Tuesday, he likely would be a possible pinch hitter.

"A lot of that comes down to how many position players we go with," manager Aaron Boone said. "... We'll talk to G, see where he's at mentally, physically and all that, and then we'll do the best we can to make the right decision."

Weathers may be an option for the postseason bullpen. He was 5-8 with a 3.60 ERA in 25 starts before feeling pain forearm pain Aug. 22 against the Toronto Blue Jays.

"I think postseason, for sure," Boone said. "Whether it's the first round or not, that will be the conversations we have in the next day or two."

Boone said the Yankees may not decide on their 26-man wild-card roster until Monday night. The roster must be submitted to Major League Baseball by 10 a.m. Tuesday.

stories.headline: Kyrie Irving has no restrictions after 19-month ACL recovery
stories.summary: Kyrie Irving said he is under no physical restrictions from the torn ACL in his left knee that sidelined him 19 months ago, an injury that he called "probably the best thing that happened to me."
stories.body:
DALLAS -- Veteran Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving says he is under no physical restrictions from the torn ACL in his left knee that sidelined him 19 months ago, an injury that he called "probably the best thing that happened to me."

"I'm ready to go out there and kick some butt," Irving, 34, said Friday during the Mavericks' preseason media day, the first time that he has addressed reporters since the March 3, 2025, injury. "I know that naysayers or some of the questions around where I'm going to be are going to be inevitable. But for me, I have the confidence of a champion.

"... This is a what-have-you-done-for-me-lately type of league, and everybody wants to see it up close. So I'm looking forward to being able to lace up my shoes and being on the court with my teammates and show everybody what I got again. It's just like riding a bike."

New team president Masai Ujiri said in terms of health that Irving is "right there."

"You hope he plays games and he gets right back into it," Ujiri said.

Irving said the time away from competitive play gave him time for reflection.

"On where I want to be as a player and most importantly where do I want to be as a man," he said. "How can people look to me to be a better leader, a better communicator, be more emotional, vulnerable. And also taking the approach of acting like my age finally. Being 34 years old, I'm going on Year 16. Been through a lot, been through a lot of ups and downs as a person. But I think me as a competitor out there, you never have to worry about me falling short of [putting] my best foot forward out there."

Irving -- and all the Mavericks -- will play for a revamped franchise after last season's 26-56 lottery finish, Dallas' worst in eight years. Ujiri was hired in early May, and he hired Dusty May in late June as coach to replace Jason Kidd. May, who led Michigan to last season's NCAA title, becomes the first coach to go directly from college basketball to an NBA head job since John Beilein left Michigan for the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2019.

Asked about being a rookie coaching Irving, May said, "Kyrie has seen and done as much as just about anyone in the association. I would expect that I'm only going to coach him when I'm able to add value."

Irving, a nine-time All-Star, will finally play alongside Cooper Flagg, last season's unanimous Rookie of the Year.

"I'm looking forward to the opportunity to grow with him," Irving said. "High-level basketball players, no matter the age -- you put us out there, we're going to win some ballgames."

Said Flagg: "Having somebody like that out there on the court with you at all times is going to be amazing. The time that we've been able to spend in the summer on the court together has been good for both of us to kind of build that connection. I'm really excited. I think it's going to be really fun to share the court."

The Mavericks on Friday announced the re-signing of Dwight Powell, who initially joined the club in December 2014 during his rookie season following a trade from the Boston Celtics.

Dallas begins its preseason with two games against the Houston Rockets in Macao, China, on Oct. 9 and 11. The Mavericks open their regular season at Houston on Oct. 21 with their home opener Oct. 24 against the Western Conference champion San Antonio Spurs.

stories.headline: Bills mark Keon Coleman, DJ Moore, Ed Oliver as questionable
stories.summary: Bills wide receivers Keon Coleman and DJ Moore and defensive lineman Ed Oliver are questionable to play against the Chargers.
stories.body:
Buffalo Bills wide receivers Keon Coleman and DJ Moore and defensive lineman Ed Oliver are questionable to play Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Coleman, who returned to practice Friday, initially sustained an ankle injury in Week 2 against the Detroit Lions, briefly leaving the field before halftime but finishing the game. Both of Coleman's ankles were taped on the practice field Friday, but he didn't sport any further braces.

Moore and Oliver also went down the night of the Lions game, with Oliver tweaking his hip pregame and Moore injuring his shoulder late in the first half. Both practiced in limited capacities this week. Moore was spotted during Friday's practice running routes and catching passes while wearing a red noncontact jersey. Oliver was a limited participant Thursday and Friday.

After Friday's practice, Moore told reporters that he is optimistic about his readiness for Sunday but that he still needs to check "a few more boxes." That includes ensuring that his shoulder feels stable and that he is able to withstand contact.

If Coleman and Moore are ruled out, the Bills' wide receiver depth will be tested. Returning contributors Khalil Shakir and Joshua Palmer started 18 combined games for the Bills in 2025. In Weeks 1 and 2, the Bills elevated veteran slot option Greg Dortch from the practice squad but used him for only four offensive snaps. Fourth-round rookie Skyler Bell has been inactive each of the first two weeks.

"I think it speaks to the types of receivers we have in the room that we have a lot of smart guys that can handle a lot of different roles," Bills coach Joe Brady said after Friday's practice. "I have a couple different plans in terms of 'Hey, if this guy's down, these are the guys that are going to be taking these plays.' So it doesn't put as much on them as it does on me, but that's part of my job with it."

Bills quarterback Josh Allen has targeted wide receivers on 32 pass attempts in 2026. Tight end Dalton Kincaid has been Allen's top option by targets (14), catches (12) and yards (225).

Defensive back Jordan Hancock (hamstring) and defensive lineman T.J. Sanders (appendectomy) will not play against the Chargers. Rookie guard Ar'maj Reed-Adams (elbow) will be questionable. Like Bell, Reed-Adams has yet to make his NFL debut.

stories.headline: Macklin Celebrini, 20, becomes youngest ever Sharks captain
stories.summary: Macklin Celebrini, 20, has been selected as the San Jose Sharks captain making him the youngest in team history to fill that role.
stories.body:
SAN JOSE, Calif. -- Macklin Celebrini was picked as captain of the San Jose Sharks on Friday, becoming the youngest player ever to fill that role for the team at the age of 20.

Celebrini takes over the spot that had been vacant since Logan Couture went down with a career-ending injury, becoming the 11th full-time captain in Sharks history.

Couture was given that role for the 2019-20 season and held it through 2024-25 even though he didn't play a single game that year because of a chronic injury to his groin and pelvic area that ended his career.

Celebrini was one of five players who rotated as alternate captains last season but now has the role for the foreseeable future. He is the youngest player to fill the leadership role, with Patrick Marleau previously holding that mark when he was named captain at age 24 in 2004. He is also the youngest current captain in the NHL, edging out 21-year-old Connor Bedard, who was named captain in Chicago earlier this month.

Celebrini has become the face of the franchise since being drafted first overall in 2024 and quickly developing into one of the game's biggest stars. He signed a five-year, $94 million extension this summer and is under contract through the 2031-32 season.

Celebrini, who turned 20 in June, has 178 career points for the fifth most ever for a teenager, and his 70 career goals are seventh best for a player before turning 20.

He had 45 goals and 70 assists last season, with his 115 points breaking Joe Thornton's franchise record of 114 set in 2006-07 and trailing Wayne Gretzky (137 in 1979-80) and Sidney Crosby (120 in 2006-07) for the most in a season for a player before turning 20.

Celebrini had the 10th-most points ever for a player who missed the playoffs, recording a point on 46.2% of San Jose goals for the second-best rate in the league behind Connor McDavid (48.9%) and the best ever for a teenager.

He also was the leading goal scorer in the Olympics, with five goals to help Canada win the silver medal.

Despite Celebrini's exploits, the Sharks still missed the playoffs for the seventh straight season. They improved by 34 points for the 10th best single-season jump in the past 30 years but landed four points out of the playoffs.

Celebrini is part of a strong young core in San Jose alongside fellow promising players like Michael Misa, Will Smith, Igor Chernyshov and Sam Dickinson. The Sharks added even more young talent this offseason with three first-round picks headlined by Swedish left winger Ivar Stenberg at No. 2. They also added North Dakota defenseman Keaton Verhoeff at No. 9 and WHL Vancouver playmaking defenseman Ryan Lin at No. 21.

General manager Mike Grier also brought in veteran reinforcements at the start of the offseason, trading for defenseman Darnell Nurse and signing defenseman Jacob Trouba and forward Mason Marchment.

stories.headline: WNBA championship and Finals MVP odds: Lynx head into playoffs as clear favorites
stories.summary: The Lynx head into the WNBA playoffs as championship favorites, with Napheesa Collier and Olivia Miles the top picks for Finals MVP.
stories.body:
The Minnesota Lynx will head into the 2026 WNBA playoffs with +115 odds to win the Finals, making them the clear favorites. That said, they were actually bigger favorites in the final weeks of the regular season, reaching odds-on status, but lengthened to their current level once the playoff picture began to take shape.

The perennially contending Las Vegas Aces are next on the odds board at +475, followed by the Golden State Valkyries at +600; the 2025 expansion team entered its second season of play with long 45-1 odds to win the championship. The Atlanta Dream (+750) and Indiana Fever (+950), who remain the biggest sportsbook liability, round out the top five.

Minnesota's title pursuit will begin with a series against the New York Liberty, who began the season favored to win the title at +220 but are now a much longer 14-1. The Liberty are +280 in their series with the Lynx, who are -350.

Sportsbooks have also released odds for Finals MVP, with Minnesota's Napheesa Collier and Olivia Miles leading the way at +320 and +350, respectively, per DraftKings lines. A'ja Wilson (+500), Gabby Williams (12-1) and Caitlin Clark (16-1) complete the top five.

stories.headline: Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained
stories.summary: The sporting world is waiting for a resolution to the hearings on Man City's charges for allegedly breaching the Premier League's financial rules. Here's what we know, and what might come next.
stories.body:
Editor's Note: This was originally published March 19, 2025. We have republished and updated this explainer of the facts -- the charges levied against Manchester City and the potential punishments -- along with insight as to the duration of the proceedings in light of Friday's news reports, which City are denying at this time. This is another explainer, from February 2026, shining light on why the process is taking so long.

What are the charges against Manchester City?

They relate to the seasons between 2009-10 and 2022-23 and cover a range of alleged breaches -- the most serious being false accounting, with respect to providing accurate financial information on revenue (including sponsorship revenue), related parties and operating costs. There are other alleged breaches, including irregularities in player and manager remuneration and, in more recent seasons, failure to cooperate with the Premier League's investigation.

If the charges relate to alleged breaches, why are they coming to light only now?

Because much of this issue relates to the "Football Leaks," when internal documents -- "leaked" say the perpetrators, "stolen or false" say some of the victims -- relating to a range of soccer-related issues were made public. German newsmagazine Der Spiegel had access to the cache of documents -- including internal emails -- and published stories accusing Manchester City of flouting financial fair play rules, which regulate how clubs can generate revenue. This led to investigations by UEFA and, later, by the Premier League.

In February 2020, UEFA's investigation found Manchester City guilty and banned them from European football for two seasons while fining them €30 million. The ban was overturned five months later by the Court of Arbitration for Sport on the basis that some charges had exceeded the statute of limitations and others were "not established" by UEFA. City were also fined €10 million for failing to cooperate with the investigation.

Why is the Premier League's case taking so long?

It's a combination of the league's own rules and the many legal challenges City have brought over the years, contesting jurisdiction and other legal matters. Consider that officials only announced the investigation in March 2019, then went years without telling anyone what was going on or even if the case was dropped. (In fact, it was Her Majesty's Court of Appeals that informed us in 2021 that it was still ongoing, following another legal challenge.)

By the time the charges were brought, in February 2023, nearly 4½ years had passed. And the hearing itself didn't begin until Sept. 16, 2024, some 19 months later. That hearing lasted 12 weeks, until Dec. 6 of last year. As for why everything took so long, we can only speculate, but it's a combination of the aforementioned legal challenges, the sheer number, volume and complexity of the charges, and the difficulty in selecting the three-person, independent arbitration panel who will ultimately issue a judgment. The arbitrators are agreed upon by both parties -- City and the Premier League.

So if the hearing ended Dec. 6, why don't we have a verdict yet?

Again, we can only speculate, because nobody outside of the panel really knows -- not even Pep Guardiola, who said he "thinks" it will be resolved by the end of March.

The panel have to come up with a verdict that both satisfies U.K. law (otherwise there is a risk of further lawsuits) and is likely to stand up on appeal by whichever party loses. There's also the possibility that the panel could issue the judgment and then, if City are found guilty on all or some of the charges, come up with sanctions at a later date, kicking the can further down the road.

If City are found guilty, what sort of punishment can be imposed on them?

Just about anything. The Premier League intentionally chose not to have set punishments for financial rule breaches because it feared clubs might be calculating enough to break rules and take the punishment if they knew ahead of time what it was going to be. So the full set of sanctions is available. It's everything from fines to points deductions (in the current season and past seasons, which would mean stripping titles) to transfer/registration bans of players to expulsion from the Premier League to -- ominously -- making "such other order as it thinks fit."

That last one could really mean anything.

But when a verdict is finally issued, if City are found guilty and a punishment set, then it's all over, right?

Ha! If only. It's extremely likely, especially if the verdict weighs heavily to one side or the other, that the side that has "lost" will file an appeal straight away, as is its right. So if the verdict comes in this month -- which, again, is by no means guaranteed -- then it will likely be another six to eight months until the appeal is heard.

If City are found guilty, their legal woes won't end there. A number of clubs have filed paperwork reserving the right to seek compensation from City for loss of income derived from missing out on European competitions and league titles if the club is found guilty. So this won't be over when the verdict drops. Far from it.

stories.headline: Embolo out of Switzerland squad over fake COVID-19 documents
stories.summary: World Cup quarterfinalist Switzerland has lost a second player from its Nations League squad because of years-old cases of fake COVID-19 documents.
stories.body:
BERN, Switzerland -- World Cup quarterfinalist Switzerland has lost a second player from its Nations League squad because of years-old cases of fake COVID-19 documents.

Breel Embolo will not join the squad in Scotland as planned, the Swiss soccer federation said Friday, due to fresh reporting in national media about his past case of obtaining forged test certificates in 2021.

- Embolo: People in Europe 'shocked' at MLS move

- Embolo debut goal gives Atlanta draw at Miami

"This decision aims to allow the team to remain fully focused on the next matches," the federation said about the Atlanta United forward.

Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka agreed with team officials last weekend to withdraw from the squad because he is implicated in an investigation of a doctor issuing fake vaccination certificates during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Xhaka, the Swiss record holder with 152 caps, admitted getting the forged document in 2022 and accepted he made mistakes.

Switzerland starts its Nations League second-tier group Saturday at North Macedonia, plays at Scotland on Tuesday, then has home games in Lucerne against Slovenia and North Macedonia.

Embolo already was suspended for the game Saturday because of his controversial red card against Argentina in the World Cup quarterfinals.

Soccer's Zurich-based rules panel, known as IFAB, later acknowledged Embolo was mistakenly sent off in a breach of video review protocol.

On Friday, the Switzerland Today outlet reported details of Embolo's financial sanction imposed last year for the previously known false test result documents.

At the World Cup, the 29-year-old Embolo scored in Switzerland's opening game -- a 1-1 draw with Qatar -- despite arriving at the tournament days later than teammates because of a visa issue with United States authorities. He also scored in a round of 32 win over Algeria.

stories.headline: Max Verstappen labels Azerbaijan GP qualifying a 'disaster,' starts eighth
stories.summary: Max Verstappen saw Red Bull's encouraging pace disappear in a "disaster" qualifying in Baku, where he will start from eighth on the grid for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen saw Red Bull's encouraging pace disappear in a "disaster" qualifying in Baku, where he will start from eighth on the grid for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Verstappen had gone quickest in final practice Friday but was unable to contend in qualifying, ending Q3 in eighth place, 1.5 seconds off pole sitter George Russell.

Verstappen's teammate, Isack Hadjar, qualified fourth, 0.6 seconds quicker than the four-time world champion.

Russell was in a league of his own at the front and looks like strong favorite for victory, but Verstappen will start Saturday's race with two Ferraris, two McLarens, the other Red Bull and Pierre Gasly's Alpine in front of him.

When asked where he might be able to fight back to, Verstappen told Sky Sports: "I have no idea. We were in a really good place the whole weekend, and we had a disaster of a qualifying because of a lot of issues. Let's see tomorrow what we can do."

In the final seconds of qualifying, Lando Norris had gone off, prompting yellow flags around the part of the track where Verstappen was.

The Red Bull driver refused to blame that, saying the pace from practice just disappeared from the moment qualifying started.

"I mean [the yellow flags were] the last thing that happened," Verstappen said. "The whole qualifying I was just lacking top speed, half a second a lap off just on top speed, even compared to my teammate. The engine was just not working. So, that's one problem.

- Mercedes' George Russell takes thrilling pole for Azerbaijan Grand Prix

- Kimi Antonelli hits wall and suffers early exit from Azerbaijan Grand Prix qualifying

- George Russell 'shocked' by Azerbaijan GP pole: 'The biggest margin in my whole career'

"Then in Q3, in my middle lap," he said, "I tried to start and the battery didn't charge, so you start the lap with half a battery, so you have to abort. Then you lose temperature because you don't have enough power.

"That then snowballs into the final lap. I started the lap, but no top speed, a yellow flag in my lap, not enough tire temperature, and then that's where you are."

Verstappen has a spotty qualifying record at Baku's circuit. Friday was the fifth time he has been outqualified by a teammate there, the most of any other venue on the calendar.

stories.headline: Suspended Swans in running for club best-and-fairest
stories.summary: Isaac Heeney is on track to be crowned the Sydney Swans' club champion after the AFL club ruled out changing the eligibility criteria for its best-and-fairest award.
stories.body:
Isaac Heeney is on track to be crowned the Sydney Swans' club champion after the AFL club ruled out changing the eligibility criteria for its best-and-fairest award.

But midfielder Heeney won't attend the awards night next week, requesting to skip the event along with Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, James Jordon and Riley Bice.

The five served a club-imposed ban from August, including the Swans' finals campaign, for breaching club standards following a post-AFL match party at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne.

Heeney and fellow ball-winner Warner are the frontrunners -- ahead of ruck Brodie Grundy -- for the club's Bob Skilton Medal, which will be presented at Sydney Town Hall next Thursday.

The club confirmed on Friday that eligibility and voting criteria will remain unchanged, leaving all players who represented the Swans this season eligible to win the award.

Heeney has won the club's last two best-and-fairest awards, while Warner finished runner-up to Callum Mills in 2022.

The AFL also opted against ruling out Heeney and Warner for the Brownlow Medal, but did not invite the pair to last Monday night's awards dinner at Crown Palladium.

The five players were made ineligible for All-Australian honours.

It comes after the five earlier this week returned to Swans headquarters for the first time since August, individually offering apologies to colleagues and teammates.

Heeney was the only player after the club meeting to address media on Wednesday, doing so with a brief statement.

"It was really nice to address the whole club," he said on Wednesday evening.

"Extremely thankful they could give us their time and understanding, so yeah, it was really good."

Warner spoke upon arriving at headquarters and said he was "just here for my exit interview".

Their club-imposed suspensions are separate from a police investigation into sexual assault allegations.

No charges have been laid, and AAP is not suggesting any wrongdoing on the part of the suspended players. Bice was subsequently cleared by police.

All five are contracted for next year, with Blakey signed to the club until 2031.

Warner and Jordon come off contract at the end of 2027, while Heeney and Bice are signed until the end of 2028.

Blakey is reportedly seeking a trade to Victorian rivals, but football boss Leon Cameron had dismissed those rumblings as "speculation" earlier this month.

Victoria Police's eight-week timeline prediction on their investigation into the Pullman Hotel incident -- which was first flagged on September 2 -- takes in the free agency and trade period from October 2 to October 14.

stories.headline: The performance bonuses for Van, Tsarukyan? Spots in P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
UFC 331 delivered some remarkable performances, a couple of which landed fighters in the ESPN pound-for-pound rankings.

One of them is not heavyweight Sean Sharaf, despite him pulling off the biggest upset in UFC history with his 12-second knockout of mega-prospect Gable Steveson. Women's flyweight Casey O'Neill produced a leading candidate for submission of the year, escaping a dangerous position to quickly armbar Eduarda Moura, but that didn't earn O'Neill a top-10 spot, either.

Both of those fighters were eye openers, but the rankings were reserved for the two winners of Saturday's headline fights.

In the main event, Joshua Van successfully defended his men's flyweight title against former champion Alexandre Pantoja, using crisp boxing and efficient grappling to secure a unanimous decision. Van moves into the men's rankings at No. 8, and Pantoja, who previously occupied that position, drops out.

Also earning a top-10 spot is co-main event winner Arman Tsarukyan, who knocked out flashy striker Mauricio Ruffy to all but secure a lightweight title shot. Tsarukyan moves in at No. 10, with former light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira falling from the rankings.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 23. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch this past weekend. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from that challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Merab Dvalishvili; 4. Ilia Topuria; 5. Alexander Volkanovski; 6. Joshua Van; 7. Arman Tsarukyan; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Pereira; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Van; 8. Gane; 9. Yan; 10. Tsarukyan.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Tom Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Topuria; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Tsarukyan.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Volkanovski; 7. Topuria; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Van; 5. Gaethje; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Tsarukyan; 8. Topuria; 9. Gane; 10. Volkanovski.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: What We Learned: Roosters game plan comes out on top; how does the league keep Marky Mark?
stories.summary: The Roosters game plan paid off against the Dolphins, there was a clear winner in the heavyweight centre clash, and the rugby league community need to find a way to keep a superstar in the sport.
stories.body:
The Sydney Roosters are through to their first NRL grand final in seven years after dishing up a 36-20 demolition of the Dolphins.

The Roosters dazzled in front of a sold-out crowd at Suncorp Stadium with Mark Nawaqanitawase leading the charge.

Here are three things we learned from Friday's preliminary final.

Roosters direct game plan plays off

From the outset it was clear that the Roosters had a plan in mind to attack the Dolphins though the middle of the field -- a healthy diet of offloads, late passes into the line and a boatload of support runners was the clear direction from Trent Robinson, and we saw it from the opening set.

The Dolphins are a team who've been able to weather the storm of other teams' middles all year, and then throw counter punches with diminutive players like Jeremy Marshall-King, Kurt Donoghue and Max Plath. But there wasn't any of that tonight, it was a dominant performance from the Roosters from the first minute, and it never really shifted.

There was some pretty justifiable logic that the Roosters would jump out to an early lead but the Dolphins, notoriously slow starters that they are, would find a way back into the contest. And while that did happen when it was 16-10, those points came from an extremely dubious Bunker decision and James Tedesco dropping a bomb. There was no period of sustained dominance for the Phins, and instead it was the Roosters who went right back on with the job after their 16-point lead was cut to just six.

At no stage in the night did the forward battle ever look like going any way other than a dominant victory for the Tricolours. A superb platform that their talented backline worked off superbly, and through to the Grand Final they go.

Robert Toia wins heavyweight clash in style

The one-on-one matchup that most of us were truly excited for heading into Friday was the centre battle between Robert Toia and Herbie Farnworth -- and it was won by the Roosters young gun in style.

Farnworth has been the best centre in the game for a couple of years now, but it was Toia who came out on top in almost all of their skirmishes. Even ignoring his powerful try, Toia was a handful every time he carried the ball up, contained his opposite man defensively and looked every bit the superstar he's grown into this year.

There needs to be some sort of collective effort from the entire rugby league community to keep Mark Nawaqanitawase

I understand that he came from rugby union originally, but how are we letting Mark Nawaqanitawase leave this sport? No player that I've ever watched does as many cool things in a single game as he does, and it's truly remarkable that the feats of athleticism he treats us to are so routine now that it isn't even shocking -- it sure is fun to watch though.

From the intercept to the absurd flick pass to the raw power for his game-sealing try (and what a pass from Victor Radley, by the way) it is a privilege to watch this guy play footy every week.

I didn't want to dedicate much column space to complaining about the Bunker, so I'll just mention it here. He was probably out when he threw that pass and it DEFINITELY went forward, but it's far easier to not fire up about that when just a few minutes earlier, Jamayne Isaako put the ball on the sideline and that was given the all clear as well. What's doing?

stories.headline: Luis Arraez (ankle) out as Phillies eye 5th straight playoff
stories.summary: Phillies second baseman Luis Arraez will sit against the Tampa Bay Rays on Friday night because of a sprained ankle. Philadelphia needs at least one win to move closer to its fifth straight playoff berth.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- Phillies second baseman Luis Arraez was not in the starting lineup against Tampa Bay on Friday night because of a sprained left ankle.

Bryson Stott will start at second base in the first game of a three-game series with the Phillies needing at least one win to move closer to their fifth straight playoff berth.

Arraez was injured after he tried to avoid a tag at first base in the Phillies' loss to Milwaukee on Thursday night.

Obtained from San Francisco at the trade deadline, Arraez stayed down for a while as trainers tended to him. He eventually hobbled off the field with assistance.

Arraez is a three-time batting champion and leads the National League this season with a .310 average.

Philadelphia leads Arizona by two games with three to play. The Diamondbacks finish the season at San Diego and own the tiebreaker over the Phillies.

The Phillies can clinch Friday with a win against the Rays and an Arizona loss to San Diego.

Philadelphia sends Cristopher Sanchez (18-6, 2.93 ERA) to the mound Friday against the AL East champion Rays, needing its ace left-hander to calm the nerves inside the clubhouse -- and silence the fans who booed the team off the field after its latest loss. The Phillies have lost 12 of 20.

stories.headline: Hurricanes sign goalie Pyotr Kochetkov to 2-year extension
stories.summary: The Carolina Hurricanes have signed goaltender Pyotr Kochetkov to a two-year extension running through the 2028-29 season with an average annual value of $3.95 million.
stories.body:
RALEIGH, N.C. -- The Carolina Hurricanes have signed goaltender Pyotr Kochetkov to a two-year extension running through the 2028-29 season with an average annual value of $3.95 million.

The reigning Stanley Cup champions announced the deal Friday, coming as the 27-year-old netminder will make $2 million this year and was due to become an unrestricted free agent. The deal will pay $2.4 million with a $1.5 million signing bonus for the 2027-28 season, then $3 million with a $1 million signing bonus for 2028-29.

"Pyotr is an incredibly talented goalie whose aggressive style fits our team very well," general manager Eric Tulsky said in a statement. "We believe in his ability to win games for this organization and are thrilled he wants to continue helping us pursue championships in Carolina."

Kochetkov missed most of last year with a lower-body injury, going 6-2 with a 2.33 goals-against average and .899 save percentage in nine appearances with Carolina. The 2019 second-round pick is set to form a tandem this year with Brandon Bussi, last year's waiver wire wonder who won 31 regular-season games and posted a shutout in Game 6 against Vegas to clinch the franchise's second Cup title.

stories.headline: Man City refuse to deny guilty verdicts in Premier League 115 breaches case
stories.summary: Manchester City on Friday did not deny there has been a guilty verdict in the majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.
stories.body:
Manchester City on Friday did not deny there has been a guilty verdict in the majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

Both the club and the Premier League have been approached by ESPN over media reports that City have been found guilty in 114 of 115 counts by an independent panel.

When contacted by ESPN on Friday, the Premier League said they wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

City also did not deny that they have been informed of the panel's decision and instead released a statement insisting that the process "remains ongoing."

One source has told ESPN that City sought an injunction Friday to block initial reporting of the verdict. City strongly denied that is the case when approached by ESPN.

It is expected that City -- which could face anything from a fine, points deduction or expulsion from the Premier League by way of punishment -- will appeal any guilty verdict.

A statement issued by City on Friday read: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC's position remains consistent with the club's statement of February 2023.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

The Premier League announced the charges against City in February 2023 following a four-year investigation.

The case was heard at an independent hearing at the International Dispute Resolution Centre in London, beginning in September 2024. It came to an end in December 2024 after 12 weeks of deliberations.

The alleged breaches of financial rules were said to have occurred over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

The Premier League's claim was centered around their belief that City did not provide "accurate financial information that gives a true and fair view of the club's financial position."

City have maintained their innocence throughout the process.

In February 2020, City were found guilty of breaking UEFA's FFP rules and given a two-year ban from European competition and €30m fine.

The suspension was lifted by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) five months later with the fine reduced to €10m.

stories.headline: Goose at Dodger Stadium during Padres-Dodgers recalls past wildlife interruptions
stories.summary: A goose slid on Dodger Stadium's field during Padres-Dodgers. It's not the first time a creature stole the show at a sporting event.
stories.body:
Sports are great. Animals are great. When the two mix, it's incredible -- sometimes.

Fans at Dodger Stadium witnessed an unlikely instance of such a mix Wednesday, when a goose flew onto the field and slid stomach first in memorable fashion.

This wasn't close to the first time an animal has become part of the game during a sporting event. There was the time a sportswriter's dog ran onto the field, interrupting a Georgia football game. And San Antonio seemingly has had as many bat encounters as "Dracula."

In honor of these amazing incidents, let's look back at some other top animal-on-field moments.

What: Goose

Where: Chicago

When: 2026

A goose patrolled the field in the bottom of the third inning during the Cubs' game against the Phillies in April. Play continued and Cubs first baseman Michael Busch recorded a hit. The baseball flew over the goose, prompting the animal to fly away.

What: Dog

Where: Tesero, Italy

When: 2026

During the Winter Olympics, a local Czechoslovakian wolfdog named Nazgul managed to get away from his owner's sight and dash onto the homestretch of the cross-country ski course in Lago di Tesero -- during the race. Luckily, there was no serious disruption to the race, a preliminary qualifying round, spare for a few seconds of confusion shaved off the times of active racers who witnessed Nazgul's trot.

"I was like, 'Am I hallucinating?'" said Tena Hadzic, a 21-year-old Croatian skier who was among the participants whose time on the homestretch portion of the race coincided with the dog. "I don't know what I should do, because maybe he could attack me, bite me."

Nazgul was quickly corralled and returned home, but not before he endeared himself to spectators and viewers back home.

What: Squirrel

Where: New York, New York

When: 2025

A squirrel emerged in the fourth inning of a Yankees-Red Sox rivalry game from behind home plate, stopping right at Jhostynxon Garcia's left foot. The rodent took off again and stopped at the third-base foul line before attempting to dig a hole in front of the mound and then scampering down the right-field line to search for a way out.

What: Squirrel

Where: Detroit, Michigan

When: 2025

The squirrel scampered around the outfield, eventually making its way to the warning track before climbing into the Tigers' bullpen during the first inning of the San Francisco Giants-Detroit Tigers match.

What: Snake

Where: Charlotte, North Carolina

When: 2025

Golfers and patrons had a front-row experience with the entanglement of sports and animals during the second round of the 2025 PGA Championship when a snake disrupted the contest.

The snake slithered its way through the course -- with the ball seemingly being its target before moving past it.

What: Bunny

Where: Norman, Oklahoma

When: 2025

During a college baseball matchup at L. Dale Mitchell Park, a bunny disrupted the contest.

With two outs in the top of the fourth inning, a bunny appeared on the third-base side. The animal started running around behind home plate before heading toward the bullpen and exiting swiftly.

What: Squirrel

Where: Oxford, Mississippi

When: 2024

Ole Miss and Oklahoma were interrupted during an SEC meeting at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium by a squirrel that disrupted the game.

Toward the end of the first quarter, a squirrel took the field on the 17-yard line before running to the end zone for a touchdown and into the tunnel away from action.

What: Insect

Where: New York City

When: 2024

Frances Tiafoe and Grigor Dimitrov had a front-row experience during their quarterfinal match at the 2024 US Open when an insect disrupted the contest.

Tiafoe pointed out the black insect during the dead ball as the ball boys sprinted onto the court and spent around 30 seconds trying to contain it by hand before the match resumed.

What: Raccoon

Where: Chester, Pennsylvania

When: 2024

The Philadelphia Union and New York City FC had a friendly creature that caused a brief stoppage in play at Subaru Park in Philadelphia.

A raccoon strolled onto the field midway through the first half. It proceeded to evade workers that attempted to remove it. However, after 161 seconds, the raccoon was taken off the field.

What: Turtle

Where: Bradenton, Florida

When: 2024

The Bradenton Marauders, a minor league affiliate of the Pittsburgh Pirates, were in the middle of their game when a turtle caused a brief stoppage in play. The surprisingly fast reptile roamed around the outfield for a bit before pitcher Magdiel Cotto managed to safely remove it from play.

What: Bees

Where: Chase Field, Arizona

When: 2024

Ahead of a game against the Los Angeles Dodgers, the Arizona Diamondbacks received a few surprise visitors behind home plate -- bees.

There was a colony forming on the protective netting behind home plate, which resulted in a delay of one hour and 55 minutes, according to the Diamondbacks.

The Diamondbacks had to call beekeeper Matt Hilton from Blue Sky Pest Control.

Hilton said he was at his son's T-ball game when he got the call. Little did he know he'd instantly become a fan favorite after taking care of the bees.

"I thought I was just here to take care of a bee problem, and people were pretty hyped up," Hilton told MLB Network.

Hilton also threw out the ceremonial first pitch.

What: Cat

Where: Angel Stadium, California

When: 2024

There's something about the last day of April and animals on the diamond.

On the same night the Diamondbacks were dealing with bees, the Los Angeles Angels and Philadelphia Phillies got a surprise visit from a cat.

In the bottom of the seventh, the cat sprinted and landed in the Phillies' dugout. Thankfully, as the broadcaster pointed out, it wasn't a black cat.

What: Squirrel

Where: Yankees Stadium, New York

When: 2023

Early in the 2023 season, a squirrel astounded the Yankee Stadium faithful when it ran across the outfield wall.

Fortunately, it appears neither fan nor squirrel were harmed in the little creature's big adventure.

What: Bats

Where: AT&T Center, San Antonio

When: 2009 -- and again in 2019

Here's the thing about bats: If you don't know much about them and what they're capable of, they're terrifying. And at AT&T Center, where the San Antonio Spurs play, they've shown up more than once.

First, we have to go to October 2009, when one bat invaded the Spurs' game against the Sacramento Kings. Luckily, the swift and speedy Manu Ginobili was still on the Spurs, and he was able to somehow swat the creature down and capture it. What's even more interesting is that this happened on Halloween night.

The bats weren't done, though.

The Spurs were taking on the Brooklyn Nets in January when the game was delayed for a few minutes by not just one, but four bats, as the staff worked to clear the animals. Clearly fans knew who was needed, as chants of "Manu, Manu, Manu" broke out in the crowd.

Sorry to break it to you, but the bats weren't done in San Antonio. A month later, during a Spurs game against the New Orleans Pelicans, another bat made its way to the floor at AT&T Center.

This time it was the Spurs' mascot, The Coyote, who was able to capture the critter with a fishing net near the scorer's table during the first quarter. The delay lasted about 90 seconds.

The bats came back again for a third time this year in March when the Spurs were taking on the Milwaukee Bucks. Again, The Coyote came to the rescue.

What: Squirrel

Where: Busch Stadium, St. Louis

When: 2011

Imagine it's your first time bursting into the spotlight, and you win the World Series.

That's how it went down (kind of) for the gray squirrel that ran across home plate at Busch Stadium during Game 3 of the National League Division Series between the Philadelphia Phillies and the St. Louis Cardinals in October 2011.

There was no delay of game, though it was evident that every player was considerably confused.

*Note: We scoured every corner of the interwebs, and there is no original video of the Rally Squirrel. It seems that 2011 was clearly a much simpler time.

The Phillies won Game 3 though, giving them a 2-1 lead in the NLDS. But the Cardinals won Games 4 and 5, clinching the series and heading to the World Series. St. Louis went on to win the 2011 World Series against the Texas Rangers in seven games with Rally Squirrel playing a role.

What: Cat

Where: M&T Bank Stadium, Baltimore and MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford, New Jersey

When: 2017, 2019

Cats are pretty nimble creatures, so it's no surprise how often they make their way into any sports venue.

In 2017, a kitten snuck down into M&T Bank Stadium to take in a game between the Miami Dolphins and the Baltimore Ravens.

Tony Romo's play-by-play is highly entertaining. But the cute cat was eventually captured by stadium staff and taken away.

The story had a happy ending, though. According to the team, a stadium employee officially adopted the stray cat and named her "Rae" -- short for Ravens.

In 2019, a black cat ran onto the field during a New York Giants and Dallas Cowboys "Monday Night Football" game at MetLife Stadium.

What: Dog

Where: Dunhill Links Championship, Scotland

When: 2012

Look, dogs and balls go hand in hand. Not only that, but Scotland is one of the most dog-friendly nations. So, it's no surprise that Dunhill Links has seen its fair share of pooches during golf play.

In 2012, however, one dog took its ball obsession a bit too far and stole Paul Casey's golf ball right off of the third hole green.

"It's the weirdest thing I've ever had happen on a golf course," Casey said. "I noticed the dog on the 12th tee and he sort of followed us down the fairway before taking a real liking to my golf ball."

The good news was that Casey was allowed to play his original ball and scored a birdie on the hole.

What: Bees

Where: Great American Ball Park, Cincinnati

When: 2019

The worst part about bees is you really have no idea which way they are going to fly. And of course, the fact that they can sting you.

There was an 18-minute delay when a swarm of bees landed at the top of the backstop screen before the first pitch of a game in May between the San Francisco Giants and the Cincinnati Reds.

Honestly, we're just glad no one got stung.

stories.headline: George Russell 'shocked' by Azerbaijan GP pole: 'The biggest margin in my whole career'
stories.summary: George Russell has said he was "shocked" when he learned he had secured pole position by the biggest margin of his career during Friday's qualifying for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
stories.body:
George Russell has said he was "shocked" when he learned he had secured pole position by the biggest margin of his career during Friday's qualifying for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Russell took pole by 0.837 seconds from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc in second place -- the largest gap between the top two in F1 qualifying since Max Verstappen secured pole by 1.244 seconds in a wet session at the 2023 Canadian Grand Prix.

The Baku pole margin is the biggest of Russell's career -- including his performances in F1's support series, Formula 2 and GP3.

"It's been a while, so it definitely feels good," Russell said of his first pole position since the Austrian Grand Prix in June. "It's probably the biggest margin in my whole career, even including F2, F3 days.

"So the lap felt really sweet, the car's been feeling great this weekend. And on a track like this, when you can hug it up like that, it feels really amazing."

Russell is currently second in the drivers' championship and 81 points adrift of Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli, who crashed during qualifying in Baku and will start from 16th on Saturday's grid.

Russell said Friday's result builds on progress he has made since F1's summer break, but still came as a surprise.

"I mean I've been filling in a great spot this whole weekend," he said. "I felt confident, I felt hooked up -- as I've said recently I'm just getting more and more on top of this car and what it requires and it's just all feeling more intuitive.

"When I crossed the line I saw the gap, I was shocked. I knew the lap was great, I had a nice slipstream at the end which gave me an extra probably tenth and a half, two tenths and it just all perfectly came together."

- Mercedes' George Russell takes thrilling pole for Azerbaijan Grand Prix

- F1 teams to expect decision on Qatar, Abu Dhabi and where 2026 season will end by mid-October

- Christian Horner on F1 return: Ferrari team principal would be 'the dream'

But Russell played down suggestions that the combination of his strong performance and Antonelli's mistake could mark a turning point in the championship battle.

"I think the performance outside today was great, but, you know, he [Antonelli] has been flawless this whole season," Russell said. "I think when you look at every championship campaign, even for the winners, there are mistakes along the way. So, yeah, I still keep on believing and keep on fighting until it isn't possible anymore.

"But I don't feel any pressure. I feel excitement every time I jump in the car now, purely because I feel more confident in myself. And we spoke about it on Wednesday here: when that confidence starts to build, it's just like this upward cycle. On the flip side, when you're on the back foot, you start losing that confidence and then you start pushing the limits more, and that's when mistakes happen.

"But, as I said, he's been flawless this season. It's the first mistake he's made in a qualifying or race this whole year. So, yeah, let's see tomorrow."

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Arman Tsarukyan elevates his position in MMA divisional rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Arman Tsarukyan put on a performance at UFC 331 that makes him all but undeniable as the next challenger for the lightweight championship.

Tsarukyan has been in this position before. In January 2025, he pulled out of a title fight because of injury one day before he was to fight for the belt. Later in the year, he was twice passed over when the UFC was booking title bouts. But Saturday's elbow to the face of Mauricio Ruffy gave Tsarukyan the impressive first-round knockout he needed to position himself as the likely first challenger of champion Justin Gaethje.

Tsarukyan's victory also boosted him above former champion Ilia Topuria to No. 2 at lightweight in the latest ESPN divisional rankings.

That is the only movement in the rankings, as Saturday's main event winner, men's flyweight champion Joshua Van, already was the top-ranked 125 pounder. Ex-champ Alexandre Pantoja remains at No. 2.

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: Roosters first into decider after Dolphins demolition
stories.summary: Sydney Roosters have ended the Dolphins' fairytale run with a 36-20 preliminary final win due largely to the unbounded magic of winger Mark Nawaqanitawase.
stories.body:
Sydney Roosters are through to their first NRL grand final in seven years after Mark Nawaqanitawase genius and a miracle Sam Walker injury comeback inspired a 36-20 demolition of the Dolphins.

The Roosters, boosted by a Nawaqanitawase intercept try against the run of play, shot out to a 16-0 lead inside 27 minutes in front of a sold-out preliminary final crowd of 52,286 at Suncorp Stadium on Friday night.

Their defensive grit on the tryline, a feature of their finals campaign, limited the damage from a mini-Dolphins comeback, but two-try hero Nawaqanitawase has a box of unlimited magic tricks that he unfurled with a wow factor rarely seen on a rugby league field.

The Roosters lost bench rake Connor Watson to a category-one HIA, upgraded by the independent doctor, in the first half and the St George Illawarra-bound utility is set to miss the grand final.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said "watch this space" when asked if Watson, who was undergoing further tests postgame, would seek an exemption to feature next Sunday.

Victor Radley's participation is also in doubt after he was reported for a hip-drop tackle on Herbie Farnworth, although Robinson felt he didn't have a case to answer given the Dolphin's legs were already grounded.

The Dolphins had won eight straight games to reach their first preliminary final, a wonderful achievement, but on this occasion it was the Roosters' big-game players who stood tallest.

Walker returned in a record-equalling 27 days from a syndesmosis injury to orchestrate the backline in a masterclass to set up a decider against either Penrith or Newcastle.

He finished with his leg strapped in ice, but Robinson declared his playmaker "fine".

Robinson will be angling for his fourth premiership win in as many attempts.

An error or a moment of magic was needed to turn an early set-for-set stalemate, and the paranormal Nawaqanitawase provided it in the 18th minute.

The rugby-bound revelation's pivotal moment was pure instinct and skill, backed with supreme confidence.

Dolphins centre Farnworth hesitated with his pass for what would have been a Dolphins try had it hit the mark. The man known as "Marky Mark" swooped, raced 90m and the Roosters never looked back.

"It's incredible to watch him play. It's pretty rare, such a care-free, instinctive player," Robinson said of his Japanese rugby-bound winger.

"We were physical getting off the line, intent post-contact and in the carry.

"It started there and ... that allowed some freedom for some individuals."

Dolphins bench impact man Kurt Donoghoe dropped the ball when he came on, then missed a tackle for a rampant Radley to score.

Walker's sublime lob for jumping Daniel Tupou had been well rehearsed and was perfectly executed.

Dolphins winger Jamayne Isaako scored tries either side of halftime, but Nawaqanitawase collected a kick and flicked it back for Robert Toia to crash over.

When Nawaqanitawase bulldozed over for his second and Walker sliced through, it was all over for the hosts.

"We started really well and did all but score on that first opportunity," Dolphins coach Kristian Woolf said.

"It was a great take from Mark ... if he doesn't take that, we score (and) we didn't quite recover."
